For any nonzero deposit amount sent into C by any sender, after the owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance becomes zero (the reference empties the contract); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a nonzero balance, violating this.

For any owner-funded nonzero contract balance and any owner address, calling withdrawAll succeeds (does not revert) and results in address(c).balance decreasing by exactly the amount withdrawn (i.e., withdrawAll transfers the current balance); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) still succeeds but does not decrease the contract balance when balance>0, so the post-call contract balance remains unchanged for some inputs.

For any nonzero amount deposited into C, when the owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance becomes zero (reference empties the contract); the mutant that changes withdrawAll to call withdraw(0) can leave a nonzero contract balance after withdrawAll for some deposits.

For any nonzero ether amount A and any depositor D, if D sends A to C (increasing address(c).balance to >= A) then after the owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance is zero; the mutant calling withdraw(0) can leave a nonzero balance, violating this.

For any caller, when the owner calls withdrawAll the contract's entire balance is transferred out (address(c).balance becomes 0); the mutant uses address(msg.sender).balance instead and can leave contract balance > 0 for some fuzzed balances.

For any owner-sent Ether amount, calling withdrawAll always empties the contract balance (address(c).balance == 0) in the reference; the mutant that calls withdraw(address(msg.sender).balance) can leave the contract balance non-zero for some fuzzed deposit amounts, so assert that address(c).balance == 0 after withdrawAll.

For any owner and any deposit amount, after the owner calls withdrawAll the contract's balance becomes zero; the mutant that uses address(msg.sender).balance instead may leave the contract with non-zero balance for some deposited amounts.

For any owner balance X and any external deposit target that reverts on receive, calling withdrawAll() by the owner must NOT revert (reference forwards contract balance to withdraw and succeeds); the mutant using address(msg.sender).balance will call withdraw with the owner's EOA balance which may be 0 and still should not cause a revert when withdraw attempts to transfer from contract — however if withdraw internally succeeds but the external target had reverted earlier when depositing, the reference still allows withdrawAll to succeed while certain mutated behavior can leave state different; we instead assert that withdrawAll always returns (does not revert) for any fuzzed deposit amount and any owner balance — the mutant will cause a revert for some inputs when combined with a reverter helper used as the deposit sender.

For any owner and any amount sent into the contract via a normal payable call, after the owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance becomes zero; the mutant calling withdraw(address(msg.sender).balance) can leave the contract with non-zero balance for some fuzzed deposit amounts and owner balances.

For any owner who calls withdrawAll when the contract has a positive balance, the reference contract always transfers the contract's entire balance to the owner (so address(c).balance becomes 0 afterwards); the mutant that makes withdrawAll a no-op can leave a positive contract balance, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller who is the owner and for any positive contract balance funded by that owner, calling withdrawAll always empties the contract balance (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that makes withdrawAll a no-op can leave a nonzero balance and thus violates this rule for some inputs.
For any owner caller and any positive contract balance, after owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance becomes zero (reference transfers all funds; the mutant no-op can leave a nonzero balance).

For any caller who is the owner and any withdrawal amount <= contract balance, calling withdraw(...) always decreases the contract's balance by that amount in the reference implementation; the mutant that uses unchecked call may fail to transfer and thus leave the contract balance unchanged for some inputs (failing callee).

For any caller who is the owner and any withdraw amount <= contract balance, invoking withdraw transfers that amount out of the contract so address(c).balance decreases by exactly that amount; the mutant that redirects withdrawals to address(this) fails because the contract balance does not decrease.

For any owner and any withdraw amount not exceeding the contract balance, calling withdraw reduces the contract's balance by exactly that amount; the mutant that redirects withdrawn funds back to the contract breaks this rule because the balance does not decrease.

For any owner-initiated withdraw of a positive amount not exceeding the contract balance, the contract's balance strictly decreases by that amount (the buggy mutant keeps funds in the contract so this rule can be violated).

For any owner-initiated withdraw(amount) that succeeds, the owner address (msg.sender) receives the funds so a direct call to withdraw by the owner results in the owner's balance increasing by the withdrawn amount; the mutant that sends funds to address(this) breaks this because the owner's balance does not increase for some inputs.
